reforms.description: The new Bank Act allows chartered banks to make conventional mortgage loans on both residential and industrial construction, increasing their ability to compete for deposits and potentially increasing the availability of mortgage funds.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By increasing the availability of mortgage funds, the reform aims to stimulate residential construction and support economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The new Bank Act has been in effect since last May.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a significant change in banking policy that could enhance the mortgage market and support housing construction.
reforms.source_quote: The new Bank Act, in effect since last May, permits chartered banks to make conventional mortgage loans on both residential and industrial construction up to 75 per cent of the value of the property.
